title: Canada to keep duty-free access for Bangladesh until 2032
excerpt: The assurance came at bilateral talks in Dhaka. Canada has given more than CAD 6.3 billion in development aid since 1972 and CAD 700 million for the Rohingya response.

image.alt: Containers stacked at the Port of Chittagong
image.credit: File photo: Moheen Reeyad / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

content:
Canada intends to keep giving Bangladeshi products preferential market access until 2032, the foreign ministry said after the sixth Bangladesh-Canada Bilateral Consultations ended in Dhaka on Tuesday (24 November), The Daily Star reported. Bangladesh is due to graduate from the least developed country (LDC) group, after which such preferences usually phase out.

The talks were co-chaired by Foreign Secretary Salahuddin Noman Chowdhury and Weldon Epp, assistant deputy minister (Indo-Pacific) at Global Affairs Canada. Trade between the two countries rose by nearly 25% to more than CAD 4 billion in 2025.

Canada has provided more than CAD 6.3 billion in development assistance to Bangladesh since 1972, the press release said. The Canadian side referred to CAD 45 million announced in October by Secretary of State for International Development Randeep Sarai for economic governance, institutional reform, private sector development, trade competitiveness and farm innovation.

Canada has given more than CAD 700 million to the Rohingya response since 2017. Both sides called for sustained international support for the Rohingya and host communities, and for conditions that allow voluntary, safe and dignified return to Myanmar. Migration, technical and vocational training and climate resilience were also discussed.

Why it matters

Canada is a major market for Bangladeshi clothing. Keeping preferences until 2032 gives exporters, and the mostly women workers they employ, more time to adjust after LDC graduation. Canada is also a long-standing funder of NGOs in health, education and the Rohingya response.

What to watch

Whether Canada formally sets out the 2032 arrangement in its tariff rules, and how the CAD 45 million is programmed.
